The 2nd accused in S.C.No.500/2020 pending before the Sessions Court, Kasaragod, arising out of Crime No.499/2020 of Vidya Nagar Police Station,
Kasargod, seeks quashment of the entire proceedings in this Criminal Miscellaneous Case filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner/2nd accused, the learned Public Prosecutor in extenso.
Also heard the learned counsel appearing for the de facto complaint, who filed an affidavit supporting quashment of the proceedings.

3. Initially, recording the statement of the minor victim, FIR was registered on 08.08.2020, alleging commission of offences punishable under 2024:KER:88227 Sections 363, 366A, 370, 354A(1)(i),
376 (2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short) and Sections 6, 5(l), 8 and 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'PoCSO Act' for short).
4.

It was also stated that,

Accordingly, the 2024:KER:88227 victim stated that molestation at the hands of AAA stated in the previous statements was false, and such a statement was given as instructed by petitioner herein to strengthen the case.

5. Relying on the said subsequent statements of the victim, the investigating officer filed final report deleting AAA, originally arrayed as the 2 nd accused from the array of accused, after arraying the petitioner as the 2nd accused, on the allegation that, he had committed offence under Section 22(1)
of the PoCSO Act.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argued that, the petitioner is absolutely innocent and he had been roped into this Crime without any sufficient materials.

It is pointed out that, going by the statutory wordings under Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act, even the subsequent 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. statements given by the victim are taken as the gospel 2024:KER:88227 of truth,
offence under Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act would not attract against the petitioner since in order to attract an offence under Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act, the person/offender is a person who makes false complaint or provides false information against the person.
It is further argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that, in this case the petitioner herein did not give any false complaint or provide any false information against any persons.
Therefore, the offence under Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act would not attract against him.
Accordingly, he pressed to quash the proceedings against him.

7. The learned Government Public Prosecutor submitted that, though initially the victim stated molestation at the hands of AAA, who is originally arrayed as the 2nd accused, in the subsequent 161 and 164 Cr.PC statements, she stated that, such a false allegation against AAA was given at the option of 2024:KER:88227 the petitioner herein.

Therefore, even though, in the stricto sensu,
offence under Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act would not attract against the petitioner in the facts of the case, offence against petitioner is made out, prima facie, under Section 22(1) r/w 17 of the PoCSO Act.

According to the learned Public Prosecutor, abetting a person to give false statement,
false complaint or false information also is an offence under Section 22(1) read with 17 of PoCSO Act.
8. The learned counsel for the de facto complainant supported quashment.

9. In order to address the controversy as to whether the petitioner committed offence under Section 22(1) of PoCSO Act, prima facie, in the facts of the present case, it is relevant to consider the ingredients which are necessary to bring home an offence under Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act.

In this regard, it is necessary to extract Section 22(1) as well 2024:KER:88227 as section 17 of the PoCSO Act;
Section 22(1) of the PoCSO Act reads as under:

sentences.text: "Any person, who makes false complaint or provides false information against any person, in respect of an offence committed under Sections 3,5,7 and Section 9, solely with the intention to humiliate, extort or threaten or defame him, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine or with both."

Section 17 of the PoCSO Act reads as under:
" whoever abets any offence under this Act, if the Act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, shall be punished with punishment provided for that offence."
10. Reading Section 22(1) making false complaint or providing false information against any person by another person, in respect of an offence committed under Section 3,5,7 & 9 solely with intention 2024:KER:88227 to humiliate or extort or threaten or defame such person, is an offence.

Here,
additional 161 and 164 statements given by the victim are the plank wherefrom the prosecution alleges that, she had given false statement against AAA as instigated by her cousin, who is the petitioner herein.
As per Section 22(2) of the PoCSO Act, when a false complaint has been made or false information has been provided by a child, no punishment shall be imposed on the child.
Therefore, no prosecution is possible against the victim herein, in view of protection under Section 22(2) of PoCSO Act.
Plainly reading Section 22(1), in the present case, the petitioner did not give false complaint or provide false information against any person under Section 22(1) of Indian Penal Code.
In the final report filed offence under Sections 17 read with 22(1) is not alleged, as pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

11. It is true that Court is having power of 2024:KER:88227 frame charge for the offence/offenses made out from prosecution records, even though the final report did not specifically allege a particular offence.

Therefore, omission in filing final report for an offence/offences disclosed from the prosecution records is of no consequence and the Court can take cognizance and frame charge for the offence/offenses made out from the prosecution records.
On reading Section 17 of PoCSO Act, in order to attract the offence abatement, a person has to abet any offence under this Act, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abatement.
12. In view of Section 17 of the PoCSO Act, when a person abets any offence under the PoCSO Act, if the Act abetted is in consequence of the abetment, is an offence.

Similarly, making false complaint or provide false information against any person by another person, in respect of an offence committed under Sections 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9 of the PoCSO Act, solely with intention to 2024:KER:88227 humiliate or instigate or threaten a person, also is an offence.

In the instant case,
as already pointed out, police did not file final report alleging commission of offence under Section 22(1) r/w 17 of the PoCSO Act.
It is relevant to note that when the victim gave initial statements on 08.08.2020, she disclosed the name of the original 1st accused as well as one AAA, as persons, who molested her.

But in a subsequent statement recorded on 18.09.2020 by the police, the version of the victim is that, her previous statement to the effect that she had familiarity with the 1st accused for one and a half years was false and the familiarity was only for a period of 5 months and she said Sathar S vs Xxx on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54353998/

sentences.text: In the same statement, she stated that the allegation that AAA also molested her, as stated in the FIS and 164 statement was false and the said false allegation was given as instructed by the present petitioner.
In the subsequent 164 statement given by 2024:KER:88227 st the victim, she stated further that the 1 accused also did not do anything, as alleged in the initial statement.

Thus the police acted upon the subsequent 164 statement as well as the 161 statement given on 18.09.2020 by the victim, to array the petitioner as the accused, who instigated the victim to falsely implicate the original 2nd accused is AAA.
It is strange to note that in the same statements, the same victim stated that the 1st accused did not do any overt act inside the car and he brought her only once in a car.
But the prosecution given a go-by to the said statements in so far as the 1st accused is concerned.
But the same is the plank where from the prosecution arrayed the petitioner as the 2nd accused.

Even though as per Section 17 of PoCSO Act abetting any offence under the PoCSO Act also is an offence, a person could not be roped in as an accused with the aid of Section 22(1) r/w 17 of the PoCSO Act, relying on the inconsistent 2024:KER:88227 versions of the victim.
That apart, indisputably offence under Section 22(1) PoCSO Act not made out from the prosecution records, prima facie.
Therefore, proceedings against the 2nd accused in the present crime, could not be justified.
Therefore, the same would require interference.
Holding so, this petition stands allowed and all further proceedings pursuant to Annexure B final report in S.C.No.500/2020, as against the petitioner/2 nd accused, stand quashed.
